load_bearing_verifications.claim: The exact Reactome apelin-13 entity is APLN residues 65-77 from UniProt Q9ULZ1; Reactome groups it with apelin-28, -31, and -36 for the receptor-binding event rather than asserting form interchangeability.

The 2019 study used a 60% fructose diet for 8 weeks, compared 2- and 12-week intraperitoneal apelin-13 treatment, and exposed 3T3-L1 adipocytes to 600 micromol/L uric acid for 48 hours; the reported serum-urate effect appeared after 12 weeks, not 2.
The accessible 2019 abstract does not report apelin-13 dose, terminal modification, supplier/purity, urinary urate, or a named renal/intestinal urate transporter mechanism.

Separate apelin-13 studies report NF-kappa-B/NLRP3-related effects in LPS lung injury, subarachnoid hemorrhage, osteolysis, and APJ-dependent stressed-macrophage myocardial injury, but none of those primary abstracts reports an MSU or gout model.

The 2024 crossover study enrolled 24 participants, 12 with chronic kidney disease and 12 matched healthy participants, and explicitly administered 1 or 30 nmol/min [Pyr1]apelin-13; urate and gout were not reported endpoints.
A six-volunteer infusion study detected intact [Pyr1]apelin-13 and multiple in-vivo metabolites, with prominent C-terminal truncation products.

limitations: The 2019 Toxicol Lett full methods were not openly accessible in this scan, so exact reagent form, dose, supplier/purity, group sizes, and unreported urate-mechanism measurements remain unresolved.
The bounded PubMed and regional queries found no direct apelin-13 MSU-crystal, gouty-arthritis, or human-gout experiment; this is a search result, not a universal absence claim.
Several disease-adjacent apelin-13 studies were screened by title and abstract; only the sources carrying the page's load-bearing claims were promoted.
Reactome and UniProt were used for identifier and pathway context, not as substitutes for primary experimental evidence.
No non-English source supplied a load-bearing claim, so the two-model translation protocol was not triggered.
